newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais upbeat on profits - paper.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais upbeat on profits - paper.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade said in a newspaper interview on Friday he expected the state-controlled bank to continue to boost its profitablity in coming years.
He said profits should rise by at least one billion francs per year at the pre-tax per-exceptional level and the net level in 1997 "should have one column more (than in 1996)," he told Le Monde.
His comments came after the bank reported on Thursday a modest 1996 net attributable profit of 202 million francs, up from 13 million, and a very strong underlying performance.
The bank's pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit in 1996 jumped to 4.5 billion francs from 1.5 billion.
The bank, poised to receive another state aid package to ready it for sale, forecast net profit would be in the "billions" of francs next year.
Referring to a newspaper report last month that the bank expected a 1997 net profit of 3.4-3.7 billion francs, Peyrelevade said it was important "not to confuse forecasts with budget targets".
"Budget targets are by necessity ambitious and do not constitute in any way a forecast," he said.
